pages.note: Audited against published CLI extension@4.1.3 (./node_modules/.bin/extension --version) installed fresh in a sandbox. The 24-entry default Chromium flag table matches DEFAULT_BROWSER_FLAGS in node_modules/extension/dist/browsers.cjs exactly, in the same order; the always-on session block, its immunity to excludeBrowserFlags, the dev-only --remote-debugging trio (devWantsCDP = mode === 'development'), EXTENSION_BROWSER_FLAGS being appended after filtering, EXTENSION_HEADLESS forcing --headless=new, the feature-switch merge, and the six Linux container detection signals all match the shipped code. Template new-browser-flags exists in `extension create --help` and in the examples repo. Only the Chromium-vs-Firefox exclude-matching description is wrong.

Every documented flag, alias and default matches `extension dev --help` on 4.1.3. Ran the failure paths: --bundle-id on a chromium target returns E_INVALID_OPTION, --parent-pid abc returns E_INVALID_OPTION, --no-reload on build returns a usage error. Watchdog constants confirmed in cli.cjs (POLL_INTERVAL_MS = 2000, HARD_EXIT_GRACE_MS = 5000). Ran `extension dev --no-browser` for 25s in the scaffold: dist/extension-js/chromium/ready.json and events.ndjson appear at the documented paths and the port walked 8080 to 8081 as the page describes. Content-script reinjection behavior needs a browser and was left unverified.

Flag table is an exact match for `extension storage --help` (areas, contexts, browsers, 5000 ms timeout, background/local defaults). Ran the three documented failure paths against a project with no live session: `storage get` gives E_SESSION_NOT_FOUND naming `extension dev --browser=chromium --allow-control`, `storage set --key foo` gives E_ARGS, `storage frobnicate` gives E_ARGS, and all three exit 1 as stated. E_STORAGE and E_TIMEOUT both exist in the shipped CODES table.

Produced two real contracts (a `build` run and a `dev --no-browser` run) in the scaffold. All fifteen always-present fields appear with the documented types, schemaVersion is 2 and schema is 1, and the shutdown case stamps status "stopped" with code "shutdown". controlPath is "/extjs-control", logsPath is the documented relative path, and managedExtensions carries {path,id} records. Read the wait loop in cli.cjs: 250 ms poll, command match, pid liveness, start-only stale acceptance gated on READY_CONTRACT_FRESHNESS_MS = 60000, E_READY_TIMEOUT on timeout. Event types compile_start/compile_success/compile_error/shutdown all exist.

`extension build --help` confirms --browser, --zip, --zip-source, --zip-filename and the chromium default. Ran `extension build --zip --zip-source`: the distribution zip lands inside dist/chromium and the source archive at dist/<name>-<version>-source.zip, exactly as documented. The AMO data_collection_permissions warning exists in the shipped bundle (missingGeckoDataCollectionPermissions) and the scaffolded manifest ships the firefox:-prefixed declaration. AMO policy dates and Firefox 140/142 parsing are external claims and were not verified.

Scaffolded the template for real with `extension create my-preact --template=preact` on 4.1.3: the template exists in the catalog, installs preact ^10.19.6, and builds clean. preact/compat aliasing is present in the shipped rspack config (node_modules/extension-develop/dist/0~rspack-config.mjs). The screenshot points at /images/examples/new-preact/screenshot.png, which exists and follows the same convention every other framework template page uses, so it is not reported.
Navigation and conceptual framing only. The one checkable class of claim is its cross-references: all nine /docs/... links resolve to existing .mdx files in the repo. No behavioral assertion to test.

Mostly browser-API guidance that Extension.js does not own. Verified the two toolchain claims that are testable: adding storage.managed_schema to the scaffold manifest emits storage/managed_schema.json into dist and rewrites the manifest key to that path, and the shipped bundle carries managed-schema validation messaging (invalidManagedSchemaStructure, isCriticalJsonFeature). The 'path outside the extension directory is flagged as a load blocker' claim is scoped to browser launch, which I could not exercise without a headful browser, so it is left unverified rather than reported.

Checked every concrete claim against the real sidebar-shadcn template in the examples checkout: it exists in the create catalog, ships React + TypeScript, @tailwindcss/postcss, a postcss.config.js identical to the documented snippet, src/components/ui/*.tsx, src/lib/utils.ts, and a components.json whose $schema, style, tsx and tailwind.css values match the page's example. The screenshot asset exists.

Both templates and both screenshots exist. Exercised the missing-Sass path for real: added a .scss import to the scaffold with no sass package installed, then ran both `extension build` and `extension dev --no-browser`. Neither auto-installs anything and neither asks for a restart, contradicting the page's behavior note. Installing only `sass` then compiles the file correctly, showing sass-loader does not belong in the reader's install command.

Conceptual mapping of change type to update mode, with almost nothing independently checkable without driving a browser. Confirmed the two things that are: E_RESTART_REQUIRED exists in the shipped CODES table, and all four next-step cross-references resolve to real pages.
